label: Ботинок
description: A 10-sentence usage card for ботинок (boot, shoe).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Ботинок' is the masculine nominative subject of the sentence. 'Этот' points at the specific shoe, and 'велик' is the short-form adjective stating it is too big. A natural fitting-room remark.

Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Ботинок' is the accusative direct object of 'надел'; as an inanimate masculine noun its accusative equals the nominative. 'Правый' agrees in the masculine accusative.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. 'Ботинка' is the genitive after the negative 'нет'. 'Второго' agrees in the masculine genitive. A common way to say one shoe is missing.

missions.phrase: К этому ботинку нужен новый шнурок.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Dative with preposition. 'Ботинку' is the dative after 'к', marking the shoe as the goal. 'Этому' agrees in the masculine dative, and 'нужен' introduces what it needs.
Strategic focus: Instrumental with preposition. 'Ботинком' is the instrumental after 'под', expressing location underneath. 'Что-то' is the indefinite subject. A natural everyday observation.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. 'Ботинке' is the prepositional after 'в', showing location inside. 'Оказался' agrees with the masculine subject 'камень'. A familiar small annoyance.
Strategic focus: Nominative plural. 'Ботинки' is the nominative plural subject. 'Эти' and 'удобные' agree in the plural, and 'очень' intensifies the praise. The standard way to comment on footwear.
Strategic focus: Accusative plural. 'Ботинки' is the inanimate accusative plural, identical to the nominative, as the object of 'купил'. 'Новые' agrees in the plural, and 'вчера' sets the time.
Strategic focus: Genitive plural. 'Ботинок' is the genitive plural after 'пары'. Note the zero ending typical of this masculine noun. A useful counting and inventory pattern.
Strategic focus: Prepositional plural. 'Ботинках' is the prepositional plural after 'на', showing location. 'Обоих' agrees in this oblique plural form. A natural way to describe dirty shoes.
